newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreign investors stay away from Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors stay away from Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Foreign investors shunned the foreign board of the Nairobi Stock Exchange on Monday and offloaded treasury bonds after the IMF halted a key aid package, bourse officials said.

Brokers said following Thursday's decision by the IMF to halt the three-year $220 million aid package amid accusations of corruption, foreign investors cancelled orders for shares, waiting for a clearer government reaction.
"Nothing at all has been traded on the foreign board. Foreigners are notable by their absence," said an official.
Monday's market was thus very quiet with the Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index falling 24.95 points to close at 3428.22, dealers said.
Bourse officials said although investors were reassured by the government's plans to cut spending and raise revenue to compensate for the lost IMF money, they were still wary of investing.
"It all depends on the government's next move," said a broker.
Turnover for the fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond was a heavy 230.4 million shillings from 250 million shillings on Friday.
Brokers said half the turnover was from anxious foreign investors offloading bonds after the IMF decision. Total bond sales in the week before the IMF decision were just 13.35 million shillings.

A broker said bonds on Monday were mainly sold in three main large deals of 100 million, 120 million and 9.5 million shillings, with trades priced at 102.60 percent from between 102.1605 and 102.00 percent.
"Foreign investors are worried about the possibility of losing on exchange rate fluctuations but I don't think we're going to see a mass exodus from the bond market," said a broker.
"Some locals are also getting a bit shakey," he added.
On the agricultural board the only shares traded were Brooke Bond which was unchanged at 123 and Rea Vipingo which remained at 8.45.
Elsewhere, Nation Printers and Publishers fell six shillings to close at 10 while Express gained a shilling to close at 69.
In the financial sector, National Industrial Credit fell to 51.50 from 60 and Kenya Commercial Bank tumbled 14 points to close at 91.
East Africa Cables edged up 0.75 to 31.25, while Kenya Breweries added 1.5 to close on 56.00.
